findings.title: Take phase 7 (WSL2 guest collector) out of version 1 and drop the 'moves after phase 2' rule; v1 shows the VM as one opaque workload, and v1's own data then gives the WSL share
findings.evidence: No component, route or schema: docs/13-build-list.md:11-35 lists components 01-25 in phases P0-P6 only; the routes (docs/13:71-83) have no ingest and say 'POST /sessions the only write' (docs/13:82). docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md:35-37 gives P7 a gate and nothing else, and docs/15:45 lets P7 jump to after P2 on a measurement. R05's fix 'The ingest API accepts a second collector' (docs/16-review-log.md:81) and docs/17-build-prompt.md:79 clash with the loopback-only, read-only API (AGENTS.md:11; lead D 'R05 ingest conflicts'). Lead D's file-based fix (guest writes raw files under /mnt/c) also fails. sqlite.org/wal.html: 'All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires all processes to share a small amount of memory'. learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/compare-versions: WSL 2 runs 'a Linux kernel inside of a lightweight utility virtual machine (VM)'. learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/filesystems: 'We recommend against working across operating systems with your files'. Lead B: the P0 rule has no denominator. Lead G: P0 cannot close because the measurement needs a working day on the owner's machine. docs/03-cli-output.md:61 shows doctor reporting 'WSL2 VM holds 3% of CPU time' from the running product.
findings.impact: As written, P7 has no design that obeys fixed rule 3: an ingest route, a token handed to a guest VM, or a WAL file shared across two kernels. The conditional move after P2 makes the phase order depend on a P0 measurement that takes a working day. Keeping it costs a design phase. Deferring it loses only the per-process view inside WSL, which v1 shows as one opaque workload anyway (docs/10-known-limits.md:11).
findings.proposed_change: docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md: delete P7 (lines 35-37). Rewrite the decision row at :45 as 'Not in version 1. The VM is shown as an opaque workload, and doctor reports its share of busy CPU time from v1's own data. A guest collector is designed after v1 if that share is large.' docs/17-build-prompt.md:79: delete 'Design the ingest path ... (phase 7)'. Delete :264's sentence and the P0 'WSL2 or Docker VM measurement' (:268). docs/16 R05: mark the ingest part as not in v1. docs/13 'Not in version 1': add 'a collector inside WSL2 or Docker Desktop'. docs/10:11: drop 'in phase 7'.
findings.cost: About 8 changed lines across docs/15, docs/17, docs/13, docs/10 and docs/16. No code.
findings.decision_question: Defer the WSL2 guest collector after v1 and let v1's opaque-VM workload measure the share (recommended), or keep P7 and its conditional move, which first needs a transport that obeys rule 3 and does not share a WAL file across the VM boundary?
findings.refutation_attempt: I searched docs/13 and docs/17 for an ingest component, route or schema and found none. I checked the file-based transport against sqlite.org's same-host WAL rule and Microsoft's statement that WSL 2 is a VM. I checked that deferral loses the measurement: it does not, because docs/03:61 has doctor report the share from the opaque workload v1 already records. It survives.

findings.title: Build tagged runs first: launcher, holder, run file and 'cost' over run files as phase 1, before the poller and store, because kernel accounting is the centre of the design and is unproven on Windows
findings.evidence: docs/reference/windows-priorities.md:83 says Job Objects decide 'whether tagged workloads can be exact, which is the centre of the design', and the item is unverified. docs/13-build-list.md:23-24 put the launcher and providers.group in P2, after P1 builds the collector, store and CLI. The launcher does not depend on them. docs/17-build-prompt.md:66: 'A tagged run is therefore accounted for even if the collector was not running'. docs/05-data-flow.md:52 says the same. The baseline has no path for group totals: aggregate() takes only kernel_workloads names and sums polled values (src/submeter/attribution/rules.py:196-216). Leads A-windows (holder must be a separate process; breakaway; assign race fixed only by PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST; nested double count; no current memory) and A-linux (systemd user scope over D-Bus with Delegate='memory pids', payload and holder leaf groups, no io.stat, page-cache memory) each change the run file, the holder and the models. On Linux the mechanism is exact on this machine: docs/review/probes/a-linux/cgroup_totals.out.txt gives 'cpu.stat usage_usec of the group: 10.677 s (-0.01%)' against wait4. On Windows nothing has run.
findings.impact: P1 is the largest phase. If the Job Object facts land in P2, P1's models, raw schema and run-file contract have to be reopened. The owner's main question, 'what does this agent run cost', waits until after P1's soak even though it needs no collector. If Windows Job Objects turn out not to nest or keep totals for this user, the design changes after the biggest investment.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md and docs/17-build-prompt.md:268-270. New P1 'Tagged runs' covers: component 13 (launcher with its detached holder), the final-totals half of 14, the run file, `submeter run`, `submeter cost --run` reading run files, and the load generator. Gate: the current P2 accuracy gate (500 sub-second children within 2% of the load generator's own accounting, final totals survive exit, run returns with the exit code while left-behind processes are still counted). The old P1 (collector, store, CLI) becomes P2. Live group reading and re-attach (the rest of 14), attribution and sessions follow in P3. docs/13:23-24: change the phase column.
findings.cost: Two phase paragraphs rewritten in docs/15 and docs/17, and two phase cells in docs/13. No code.
findings.decision_question: Reorder so that tagged runs (launcher, holder, run file, cost) are phase 1 and the poller and store phase 2 (recommended), or keep the brief's order?
findings.refutation_attempt: I looked for a dependency of the launcher on the collector or store and found none: it writes its own run file (docs/17:66, docs/06:17). I looked for a reason P1 must precede it: the P1 gate needs no groups. I checked whether kernel accounting is already proven: on Linux at probe level (-0.01%), on Windows only in documentation. It survives.

findings.title: Cut hot and cold sets: read every process every tick, slow only the costly fields, and default the active interval to 2 s
findings.evidence: Lead B: docs/review/probes/b-measurement/hot_cold_sampler.out.txt. Hot-only ticks 'credited 30.0 CPU-s of 94.8 (32%), processes started 1620, exited 1620 (truth: 0 and 0)'. Carrying counters forward gives 'cores p50 0.49, p95 11.62 (truth 1.58 both), capacity 8'. docs/review/probes/b-measurement/model_tables.out.txt section 3: 'whole tick + raw store 36.0 ms 0.25s 14.41% (over) 1s 3.60% (over) 5s 0.72% (ok)'. The only in-budget figure at 1 s ('10% of 300 processes hot ... 1s 0.68%') assumes cold processes are not read each tick, which is variant A, the one that credits 32%. reconcile_terms.out.txt: 'the smallest use that can be seen in one second is 1% of a core', so hot_cpu_threshold 0.5% (docs/08-configuration.md:65) cannot be resolved. docs/17-build-prompt.md:71 already says the Windows bulk call returns counters 'for every process'. model_tables section 1: measured capture of 82 ms children at about 1.13 s is about 2.9%, so moving from 1 s to 2 s loses almost nothing that polling catches.
findings.impact: Built as specified, hot and cold sets either lose about two thirds of CPU time and invent starts and exits, or report more cores than the machine has (lead B, critical). Making them correct (per-process intervals, lead B option 2) is a sampler redesign that saves only the per-process work of cold rows. Their cost saving exists only in the variant that is wrong.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md:71: replace 'Keep a hot set ... cold interval' with 'Read cumulative counters for every process every tick. Read the costly fields (USS or PSS, command line, working folder) on the slow cadence.' docs/17:170-174 and docs/08-configuration.md:61,63,65: active_interval default 2s, and delete cold_interval and hot_cpu_threshold. Adaptive mode moves between active (2s) and idle (5s) only. docs/04-features.md:8, docs/05-data-flow.md:12,84 and docs/13-build-list.md:17: drop 'hot and cold sets'. docs/08 explorer: replace its formula with the measured per-tick cost. src/submeter/core/config.py: remove the two fields. collector/sampler.py: remove hot_keys (lines 104-112). P0 confirms the default on the owner's machine: at 452 processes the same figure is 54 ms, 2.7% at 2 s and 1.08% at 5 s, so idle may need 10 s.
findings.cost: About 12 document lines and about 20 lines of code removed.
findings.decision_question: Cut hot and cold sets and move the default active interval from 1 s to 2 s (recommended; measured 1.8% of a core per 300 processes on Linux), or keep 1 s and schedule the per-process-interval sampler redesign (lead B option 2)?
findings.refutation_attempt: I tried to keep the feature by finding a correct variant that saves cost. Reading every process's CPU every tick (lead B option 1) keeps the per-process delta and attribution work that makes up about 20 of the 36 ms. The remaining saving covers only the costly fields, which uss_interval already slows. I recomputed 36.0 ms / 2000 ms = 1.80% < 3%. Windows is unmeasured, which is stated. It survives.

findings.title: Defer phase 6's MCP server; an agent gets its own cost from `submeter cost --json`
findings.evidence: docs/04-features.md:38 says the MCP server is there 'so an agent can ask what it is costing'. docs/13-build-list.md:59 lists `cost`, and docs/17-build-prompt.md:197 says 'every command accepts --json with a stable schema'. The agents spawn git, rg and pytest (docs/17:60), so they can run a command. MCP needs a dependency that is not approved (AGENTS.md:46: pydantic, psutil and typer only; uv.lock has no mcp package; grep count 0). Lead G: SDK or a hand-written JSON-RPC server, and the transport is unspecified. Lead D: 'never returns command lines' is a courtesy, not a boundary, and documents disagree on what it withholds. Lead F: no API route serves cost or runs. The P6 gate (docs/15:33) is 'an agent can retrieve its own cost', which the CLI satisfies once the launcher sets a run id in the command's environment (lead G).
findings.impact: MCP adds a phase, a dependency, a transport and a security wording problem for something the CLI already provides to the same agents.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md:35 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:214: move component 25 to 'Not in version 1'. docs/15:31-33: P6 gate becomes 'an agent can retrieve its own run's cost with `submeter cost --run "$SUBMETER_RUN" --json`, and the output contains no command line'. docs/04:38: say the CLI serves agents in v1. docs/08:107 and config.py Api.mcp_enabled: remove. Keep `report` (24) only as the dashboard's substitute (see the CLI-first finding); otherwise defer it too.
findings.cost: About 6 changed document lines and a 2-line config removal.
findings.decision_question: Defer the MCP server after v1 and serve agents through `submeter cost --json` (recommended), or keep it in v1 with an approved SDK or a hand-written stdio server?
findings.refutation_attempt: I checked whether an MCP-only capability is needed: docs/04:38 and docs/15:33 ask only for cost retrieval, which `cost --json` gives. I checked whether agents can call a CLI: they run shell commands (docs/17:60). It survives.

findings.title: Drop Parquet export; export JSON and CSV
findings.evidence: docs/17-build-prompt.md:142 and :204, and docs/13-build-list.md:63 ('export Parquet or JSON'). No job reads an export: docs/01-overview.md:7,11,16 name table, cost, why, history, findings and diff. AGENTS.md:46 allows three runtime dependencies, and uv.lock has no pyarrow (grep count 0). Lead G names pyarrow as the needed package. The stored files are already SQLite, an open format.
findings.impact: Adds a large dependency that needs approval for a convenience no job needs.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md:142 'Export to JSON and CSV'. :204 and docs/13:63: 'export to JSON or CSV'. docs/13 'Not in version 1': add 'Parquet export'.
findings.decision_question: Export JSON and CSV only in v1 (recommended), or approve pyarrow for Parquet?
findings.refutation_attempt: I searched docs for any consumer of Parquet (a gate, a job, a report) and found none. CSV and JSON need only the standard library.

findings.title: Cut the minute tier: keep raw (48 h) and hourly (kept); run the leak check on raw and baselines on hourly
findings.evidence: Only two checks read minute buckets (docs/06-storage.md:64-65): the leak check, '2 to 48 h back', which lies inside raw retention, and the baseline, 14 d back. Lead B: on minute buckets about 4% of ordinary minutes are flagged; the docs/07:31-36 example uses daily peaks. growth.theil_sen already thins input to 300 points (src/submeter/analysis/growth.py:26-33), so 2 h of raw rows is cheap to fit. roll_up takes any width (src/submeter/store/rollup.py:100-110), so hourly buckets can be built from raw, as docs/17:123 and R13 already say. Probe docs/review/probes/h-scope/minute_tier_reach.out.txt (choose_tier with default retention): 'windows answered by the minute tier: 11 of 21', 'minute tier is chosen for spans over 33.3333 min and up to 33.3 h'; 2 d, 7 d and 30 d windows already come from 'hour/3600s'. Minute-file leads that disappear: C (open file blocks delete; schema versions across 37-day files; bucket finality with long samples; budget 5-6x estimate) and F (hourly built from minute in code against raw in the brief).
findings.impact: A third file kind, with its writer, retention, migration window and membership rules, serves no job's acceptance test. Several storage leads exist only because of it.
findings.proposed_change: docs/06-storage.md:11-19,48-67,111: two tiers plus stored totals. Leak check reads raw workload rows; baseline (if kept) reads hourly. docs/17-build-prompt.md:105 delete the minute files; :154 'Run this check on raw workload rows'; :156 'from hourly buckets'. docs/04-features.md:21 and docs/05-data-flow.md:19,35,48: two lifetimes. docs/13-build-list.md:20,40: drop rollup_1m and the minute file. docs/08:81: delete retention.minute. src/submeter/store/query.py: inside raw retention answer from raw merged to wider steps, otherwise hourly. store/files.py: remove minute_file and expired_minute.
findings.cost: About 15 document lines in 6 files; about 30 lines of code removed or simplified in query.py and files.py.
findings.decision_question: Go to two tiers, raw and hourly (recommended; lost: windows of 34 min to 33 h that ended 2 to 30 days ago drop from 1-minute to 1-hour resolution), or keep the minute tier?
findings.refutation_attempt: I listed every reader in docs/06:59-67 and ran choose_tier over a grid to see what the minute tier answers. It answers medium windows only, and no gate or job acceptance depends on 1-minute resolution older than 48 h. Inside 48 h, raw can be merged at query time. Whether that query fits a time limit was not timed (timing ban), so it is under not_checked.

findings.title: Defer baseline anomaly and slow growth; v1's trend job is leak detection, diff and hourly history; the Windows I/O verdict and `why` must stop depending on undefined baselines
findings.evidence: Both checks say nothing for 7 days: docs/08-configuration.md:89-90 (slow_growth.window 7d, baseline.learning_period 7d), docs/07-analysis.md:35. So no builder can test them on real data, only on fixtures. Lead B: slow growth cannot fire (no threshold of its own; 6 daily minimums in a 7-day window); the baseline table matches neither rule nor code; there is no floor default; minute buckets give 4% false flags. Lead F: idle and active are never defined, and the window is stated two ways. Coupling into job 2: docs/07-analysis.md:99 Windows I/O-bound is 'Disk queue and latency above baseline', and docs/03-cli-output.md:32 shows 'run queue 2.3 per core baseline 0.4'. Baselines are specified only per workload (docs/07:29-36, docs/17:156), so these system baselines are defined nowhere. 'Spike, swap storm' have one line each and no rule (docs/17:158; no code: grep -rn spike src finds only a docstring). Job 3's acceptance is the leak alone (docs/01-overview.md:18). The hourly tier is kept forever (docs/06:15), so deferred detectors can later be fitted on history recorded from day one.
findings.impact: Two detectors that need tuning on weeks of real data would be built against fixtures, with known defects in each (leads B and F). Job 2's Windows I/O verdict cannot fire until an undefined baseline exists, at least 7 days after install.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md:27: v1 detectors are leak and process count. Baseline anomaly, slow growth, spike and swap storm move to 'Not in version 1', or each gets a one-sentence rule. docs/04-features.md:30, docs/08:89-92, docs/17:155-156 and docs/15:21 (drop 'a leak too slow for the hourly check'): defer. docs/07-analysis.md:99: Windows I/O-bound uses absolute disk queue and latency thresholds, tuned against fixtures like the other rows. docs/03:32: drop 'baseline 0.4'. Keep growth.usual_range and daily_minimums as tested library code. docs/17:15: replace 'three jobs of equal weight' with an order for cuts: attribution, then live diagnosis, then trends.
findings.cost: About 12 changed document lines in 6 files. No code removed.
findings.decision_question: Defer baseline anomaly and slow growth (and rank the jobs attribution > diagnosis > trends for cuts) (recommended; nothing is lost from the data because hourly history is kept), or keep both in v1 and schedule the B and F fixes?
findings.refutation_attempt: I searched docs for a system-metric baseline (disk latency, run queue) and found only per-workload baselines. I checked whether job 3's acceptance needs either detector: it names only the leak (docs/01:18). I checked whether deferring loses data: no, because hourly history is kept. It survives.

findings.title: Phase 0 should be three decision probes on the owner's machine plus CI; remove the VRAM drift, WSL working-day and 'doctor correct on both' items
findings.evidence: docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md:9 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:268 ask P0 for doctor 'correct on both' (no oracle, lead G), a VRAM drift check (needs a GPU; lead G: hosted runners have none), the WSL share over a working day (lead B: no denominator), and 'the cost of one full sample' with only the psutil provider in hand (lead B: the switching rule is undefined; docs/review/probes/measure/snapshot_cost.out.txt: psutil 74.6 ms per 300 against a direct /proc read of 7.5 ms). GitHub docs (docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners): 'Windows virtual machines are configured to run as administrators with User Account Control (UAC) disabled', so CI cannot show what a standard user can do. Facts that can change v1's design and exist only on the owner's machine: Job Objects (docs/reference/windows-priorities.md:83; lead A-windows: the name survives only while a handle is open, so the holder design depends on it), bulk-call cost (docs/11-language.md:21), and autostart without elevation (leads D and G, suspected).
findings.impact: As written, P0 cannot be closed by a builder, and its measurements do not decide anything that is still open. The three facts that can change v1 (holder design, Python or Rust and the default interval, how `daemon install` works) are tested late or never.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15:9 and docs/17:268. P0 = (1) the four checks and platform_check.py on the owner's machine as the signed-in standard user; (2) CI on both OSes for portable tests; (3) three owner-run probes with saved output: Job Object create, nest under the terminal's job, accounting after children exit, reopen by name from a second process after the creator exits; a bulk-snapshot prototype timed at the owner's process count; registering per-user autostart without elevation (scheduled task, else an HKCU Run value). Gate: each probe's output is saved and the plan's dependent choice is recorded. The VRAM check goes with the P5 trim, the WSL share with deferring P7, and doctor grows with each provider.
findings.cost: Two paragraphs rewritten. Three probe scripts of about 100 to 200 lines each, written by the builder and run by the owner.
findings.decision_question: Replace P0's VRAM, WSL-day and full-matrix items with the three decision probes on the owner's machine (recommended), or keep P0 as written?
findings.refutation_attempt: I checked whether each removed item decides anything in v1. VRAM only gates leak checks on VRAM, which is deferred by the P5 finding. WSL decides P7, which is deferred. The full doctor matrix has no reference to check it against. Each probe I kept decides a v1 design choice named by a lead. It survives.

findings.title: Trim phase 5 to GPU load by engine; defer per-process VRAM, connections, battery level and Linux temperatures; throttling stays with the system provider
findings.evidence: Metric catalogue consumers: docs/06-storage.md:88 'VRAM ... GPU verdict. Leak checks only once validated'; :89 'Connections ... Workload table' (no job or verdict). The verdict (docs/07-analysis.md:95-102) uses GPU engine load and frequency, not connections, battery or temperature on Windows (temperatures are unavailable there, docs/10-known-limits.md:14). Frequency is already in component 06 at P1 (docs/13-build-list.md:16), which duplicates 'throttling' in 23 (docs/13:33). docs/17-build-prompt.md:273: 'Hardware you do not have is tested from recorded fixtures', so P5 providers may ship never having run on real hardware, against priority 1 'Never show a wrong number' (docs/17:29). Lead A-linux: Linux per-process GPU sources in docs/09 are wrong. Lead B: the thermal rule fires on any turbo CPU. Lead G: CI has no GPU. docs/15:9: VRAM drift check in P0.
findings.impact: A phase of providers is built mostly from synthetic fixtures for metrics no job reads. One P0 gate item (VRAM drift) needs owner hardware for a metric v1 will not use for leak checks.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md:33: component 23 = 'GPU load by engine type, machine-wide and per process, busiest as headline'. docs/13 'Not in version 1': per-process VRAM, connections per process, battery level (keep only the on-battery flag the cadence uses), temperatures. docs/15:27-29 and :9 (drop the VRAM check), docs/01-overview.md:23, docs/04-features.md:10, docs/17:85-90,176, and docs/08-configuration.md:69-70 (delete thermal_interval and network_interval; frequency is read on the main tick).
findings.cost: About 10 changed document lines and 2 setting fields removed.
findings.decision_question: Keep only GPU load from the extra telemetry in v1 (recommended), or keep VRAM, connections, battery and temperatures?
findings.refutation_attempt: I searched every doc for a consumer of connections, battery level, VRAM or temperature that a job's acceptance needs. Only the workload table column and an untrusted VRAM gauge use them. GPU load is kept because it feeds a verdict class. It survives.

findings.title: Shrink the settings surface: settings read at start (reload = restart), no profiles, no per-session interval; 13 of the 42 setting rows go with the other cuts
findings.evidence: Hot reload: docs/13-build-list.md:12, docs/17-build-prompt.md:187, docs/08-configuration.md:5. Per-session interval: docs/08:74, docs/17:190. Profiles: docs/08:117, docs/17:180, src/submeter/core/config.py:277-306. Lead G: no channel carries reload, stop or a session's interval, and Windows has no signal to send. Lead F: epochs stated five ways, with adaptive, guard and session-override changes as epochs. Lead F: profile selection unspecified. Lead E: unselected profiles are not validated. Rows counted in docs/08: sampling table 13 (:60-72), other settings 29 (:80-108). Rows removed by the other findings: cold_interval, hot_cpu_threshold, thermal_interval, network_interval, retention.minute, slow_growth.window, the three baseline.*, quiet_hours, channels, port/mcp_enabled, units/default_range.
findings.impact: Hot reload and session overrides each need a control channel and mid-run epoch rules that the brief does not have. Profiles add an unspecified selection rule.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md:187-190: 'Settings are read when a program starts. `submeter config reload` restarts the collector and server; the restart starts a new epoch if the settings, rules, version or hardware differ from the last one.' Delete the session interval override (docs/08:74, docs/17:190) and profiles (docs/08:117, docs/17:180). Per-machine settings come from `--file` or SUBMETER_HOME. docs/13:12: drop 'hot-reloads'. config.py: remove profile handling. This also settles lead F's epoch definition: only the start of a program begins an epoch.
findings.cost: About 8 document lines; about 20 lines of config.py removed.
findings.decision_question: Read settings only at start, drop profiles and the per-session interval in v1 (recommended; lost: a change without a restart, which costs a few seconds' gap, and one file shared across desktop and laptop), or keep all three and specify the control channel?
findings.refutation_attempt: I checked whether any job's acceptance needs a reload without restart or a per-session interval: none does. A restart only leaves a short uncovered interval (sampler.py:50-51 returns no batch for the first snapshot), which coverage shows as uncovered, not as zero. It survives.

findings.title: Make version 1 CLI-first: defer the HTTP API, WebSocket and web dashboard; the server keeps rollups, retention and detectors with no network listener; charts come from `submeter report`
findings.evidence: Every job already has a CLI surface: docs/01-overview.md:7 (`submeter cost`), :12 (`submeter why`), :16 (`submeter diff`). No job gate needs the dashboard: the P3 gate is `why` under 2 s (docs/15:21), and the P4 gate (docs/15:25) is the only dashboard gate. The baseline CLI already reads libraries directly, not an API: src/submeter/cli.py:21-27 import attribution, sampler, provider and store.files, while docs/05-data-flow.md:50 routes the CLI through the API. Leads that exist only because of the API, dashboard or MCP: D 'named stack and dashboard mock contact other hosts' (critical, rule 3), D token carriage, D port 8787 squatting, D MCP courtesy, F 'API routes serve neither cost nor runs', F chart library and dependencies, G 'at least four runtime dependencies beyond the three AGENTS.md allows' (AGENTS.md:46). Leads that exist partly because of them: G interface guesses (WebSocket messages), G 'P2 and P3 gates depend on the P4 API', C 'long-lived reader grows the WAL', D workload names reaching dashboard HTML.
findings.impact: Two components, a phase, the only network listener in v1, a token system and four or more dependencies serve none of the three jobs' acceptance tests. They carry a critical rule-3 risk and about seven leads' worth of fixes.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md:30-31: move server.api and web to 'Not in version 1'. Delete `config rotate-token` (:64) and the 'API routes' list (:69-83). docs/15:23-25: replace P4 with 'Report: `submeter report` writes one self-contained HTML file with the chart library inlined and a meta CSP of default-src none; a 30-day report comes from the hourly tier and names it; the file references no other host'. docs/01:22, docs/04:35-38, docs/05:44-50 and docs/17:21,38-39,148,195-214,254,272: the CLI reads store files read-only; there is no listener, port or token in v1. docs/08:107-108: delete the api and ui rows.
findings.cost: Document edits in about 7 files (roughly 30 lines). No code, because the baseline has no API code.
findings.decision_question: Ship v1 as collector + background server + CLI + static HTML report, with the live dashboard and API in a v1.1 once the numbers are proven (recommended), or keep the dashboard and API in v1 and take the token, Host/Origin, asset and dependency fixes from leads D, F and G?
findings.refutation_attempt: I checked each job's 'Where you see it' line for a surface only the dashboard gives: each names a CLI command too. I checked whether `why` or `cost` need the server: the baseline CLI is library-direct. What is lost: a live auto-refreshing view and the process-tree drill-down (a CLI `top` tree can replace it). It survives as a decision, not a defect.

findings.title: Build one operating system's platform layer in version 1; the other OS keeps the psutil provider (polled, labelled) and portable CI
findings.evidence: Each platform phase doubles: P1 has 04 Windows bulk and 05 Linux procfs (docs/13-build-list.md:14-15); P2 has Job Object and cgroup (docs/13:23-24). docs/17-build-prompt.md:266: 'you can only run one OS yourself'. prompts/01-execution-prompt.md:3 puts the build on 'my Windows 11 work computer', while this review ran on Linux. GitHub docs: 'Windows virtual machines are configured to run as administrators with User Account Control (UAC) disabled', so CI cannot verify the standard-user behaviour that fixed rule 2 depends on. The two kernel paths differ in design, not only in API. Linux on this machine: docs/review/probes/a-linux/cgroup_scope.out.txt 'passing memory down while this process is in it: refused (Device or resource busy)' and, without a user bus, 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'; cgroup_totals.out.txt 'io.stat NO'. Windows: lead A-windows (separate holder, JOB_LIST attribute, breakaway, no current memory). docs/reference/windows-priorities.md:100: 'Linux needs its own pass later ... None of that code exists yet.' Leads: about 16 A-linux and 12 A-windows findings, each OS-specific.
findings.impact: Every platform phase carries two designs and two gates, and one of them can be verified only in CI, as administrator on Windows. A gate passed in CI can then fail on the owner's machine under a standard user.
findings.proposed_change: docs/01-overview.md:25 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:21: 'Version 1 builds the platform layer (bulk provider, kernel accounting, system counters, autostart) for one OS. The other OS runs the portable psutil provider, labelled polled, where `submeter run` reports that tagged runs are unavailable and runs the command polled. Its CI job runs the portable tests.' docs/13: mark 04 or 05 and the OS half of 13 and 14 as 'after v1'. docs/15: gates name one OS.
findings.cost: About 8 changed document lines. No code; provider interfaces stay as they are.
findings.decision_question: Which OS gets the v1 platform layer? Recommended: the OS the build sessions run on and the owner uses daily. Per prompts/01:3 that is Windows. If the build will in fact run on this Linux machine, as the review did, choose Linux, whose kernel path is already shown exact here (cgroup_totals: -0.01%). Or keep both OSes in v1?
findings.refutation_attempt: I looked for shared code that would make the second OS cheap. Only the interfaces are shared, and the kernel-accounting designs, memory units and I/O availability differ (probes above). I checked whether CI can stand in for the second OS: on Windows it runs as administrator. Whether the owner uses Linux at all is not known, which is why this is a decision.

findings.title: Defer desktop notifications; in v1 alert rules raise findings that `why`, `top` and the report show
findings.evidence: docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md:47 settles 'Dashboard and desktop notifications only'. docs/13-build-list.md:32 component 22 includes 'desktop delivery'. pyproject.toml's runtime dependencies are pydantic, psutil and typer only, and AGENTS.md:46 requires approval for more; lead G lists a PowerShell or notify-send subprocess as the alternative. Lead G: hosted CI has no user session to test delivery. Lead F: quiet_hours is never specified (docs/08:98). Lead A-linux: the built-in 'memory nearly full' rule reads 264-274% on Linux and would notify all the time.
findings.impact: A delivery mechanism that cannot be tested in CI and needs a subprocess or a dependency, for a channel whose main built-in rule is wrong on one OS.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md:32: component 22 = 'Rule evaluation and cooldowns; a firing rule raises a finding'. docs/15:47: 'Findings only in version 1; desktop delivery later'. docs/08-configuration.md:98-99 and docs/17:180: delete quiet_hours and channels.
findings.cost: About 5 changed document lines; 2 config fields removed.
findings.decision_question: Deliver alerts as findings only in v1 (recommended; lost: a push notice when you are not looking), or keep desktop notifications and approve a mechanism?
findings.refutation_attempt: I checked whether any job's acceptance names a notification: none does (docs/01:8,13,18). I checked whether the stdlib or the three approved packages offer delivery: pyproject lists none. The claim that a subprocess is needed rests on lead G.

findings.title: The floor of version 1: what must not be cut, and the phase list that results from the cuts above
findings.evidence: Job 1 acceptance (docs/01-overview.md:8): parts sum to the whole within 2% and tagged workloads match the kernel within 2%. That needs the launcher, holder and run file (R01), one bulk provider, attribution with the four fixed buckets and reconciliation (R07; lead B wants a 'not seen by polling' term), run and session or period totals that outlive raw (R26), and redaction with exe_only as default (lead D). Job 2 (docs/01:13): a verdict in under 2 s with Inconclusive. That needs component 06 (per-core load, frequency, commit, paging, run queue, PSI) and 18, reading raw. Job 3 (docs/01:18): the leak flagged within 2 h. That needs raw plus hourly tiers with coverage (gap fixes from leads B, C and E), the leak detector, diff and epochs. Priority 2 (docs/17:30) needs the overhead guard and self-cost. The trend data needs autostart (lead A-windows: task settings) and the disk budget.
findings.impact: Without this floor stated, cuts could reach a part a job's acceptance depends on.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md, if the recommendations above are accepted. P0 decision probes and CI. P1 tagged runs (launcher, holder, run file, `run`, `cost --run`, load generator). P2 collector and raw store (one OS's bulk provider, system counters, full snapshot each tick at 2 s/5 s, gap rules, `top`, reconciliation, overhead guard). P3 attribution and history (rules, live groups and re-attach, sessions, hourly rollup from raw, retention, budget, backups, `store status`). P4 analysis (verdict and `why`, leak, process count, diff, alert findings). P5 report and GPU load. After v1: dashboard and API, MCP, WSL guest collector, baselines and slow growth, VRAM, connections, battery, temperatures, Parquet, desktop notifications, the second OS's platform layer. Six phases instead of eight.
findings.cost: One rewritten phase list in docs/15 and the matching lines in docs/17:268-275.
findings.refutation_attempt: For each item in the floor I traced it to a job acceptance line or priority in docs/01 or docs/17, and I did not keep an item that no acceptance line needs.

nothing_found: Python as the language: the measured direct /proc read is 7.5 to 15.5 ms per 300 processes and the collector-shaped process holds 39 MB resident (model_tables.out.txt sections 3-4). The tick's extra cost is Python work after the read, which a 2 s active interval absorbs (1.8%). No language change is proposed; Windows is unmeasured.
Three separate programs (collector, server, launcher): the split is what lets the launcher ship first and the collector be replaced later. No cut proposed.
Sessions: kept. After raw expires they are the only exact cost for a period that does not start and end on the hour (R26).
Hourly top-10 executables per workload (exe_1h): kept, because job 3's 'what inside the browser grew' needs it (R28). Its name-stability problem is lead A-linux's.
Disk budget, backups and one-instance locks: kept. Their defects are storage and baseline findings, not scope.
Adaptive cadence: kept as two intervals (active and idle), because a full tick at 2 s costs 1.8% against the 1% idle limit. Hot and cold sets are cut instead.

measurements: Whole tick + raw store, Linux, 300 processes (model_tables.out.txt): 36.0 ms. At 1 s that is 3.60%, at 2 s 1.80% (recomputed), at 5 s 0.72%. Scaled to 452 processes: 54.2 ms, which is 2.71% at 2 s, 1.08% at 5 s and 0.54% at 10 s. Hot set at 10% gives 0.68% at 1 s, but only when cold processes are not read, which is the variant that credits 32% of CPU (30.0 of 94.8 CPU-s). The carry-forward variant reports a p95 of 11.62 cores on an 8-core machine. minute_tier_reach probe (choose_tier, raw 48 h, minute 30 d, 2000 points): the minute tier answers 11 of 21 windows at a 1 s raw interval and 10 of 21 at 2 s, for spans of 33.3 (or 66.7) min to 33.3 h. Spans of 2 d, 7 d and 30 d come from the hourly tier. Settings rows in docs/08: 13 + 29 = 42, of which 13 go with the cuts. Leads that exist only because of the API, dashboard or MCP: 7 wholly, 4 in part. Linux cgroup run total against wait4: -0.01% (a-linux cgroup_totals).
